title_en: Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Jurisdiction over First-instance Intellectual Property Civil and Administrative Cases

articles.content_en:
Article 1 First-instance civil and administrative cases involving ownership and infringement disputes of invention patents, utility model patents, new plant varieties, integrated circuit layout designs, technical secrets, and computer software, as well as monopoly disputes, shall be under the jurisdiction of the Intellectual Property Court, the intermediate people's courts of the capitals of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the intermediate people's courts designated by the Supreme People's Court.
Where the law provides for the jurisdiction of the Intellectual Property Court, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 2 First-instance civil and administrative cases involving ownership and infringement disputes of design patents and cases involving the recognition of well-known trademarks shall be under the jurisdiction of the Intellectual Property Court and intermediate people's courts; with the approval of the Supreme People's Court, they may also be under the jurisdiction of primary people's courts, except for administrative cases concerning design patents.
First-instance intellectual property cases other than those provided for in Article 1 and the first paragraph of this Article, where the amount in controversy exceeds the amount determined by the Supreme People's Court, or which involve administrative actions of a department of the State Council, a local people's government at or above the county level, or customs, shall be under the jurisdiction of intermediate people's courts.
Where the law provides for the jurisdiction of the Intellectual Property Court, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 3 First-instance civil and administrative intellectual property cases other than those provided for in Articles 1 and 2 of these Provisions shall be under the jurisdiction of the primary people's courts determined by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 4 For novel, difficult and complex, or legally instructive intellectual property civil and administrative cases, the higher people's court may, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the procedural law, upon the request of the lower people's court or on its own initiative, decide to try the case at a higher level.
If it is truly necessary to transfer a first-instance intellectual property civil case under its jurisdiction to a lower people's court for trial, the court shall, in accordance with Article 39, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, report to its superior people's court for approval on a case-by-case basis.

Article 5 Where, in accordance with these Provisions, the Supreme People's Court is required to determine or adjust the standards for the amount in controversy or the regional scope of jurisdiction, such matters shall be reported level by level to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

Article 6 These Provisions shall come into force on May 1, 2022.
Where any judicial interpretation previously issued by the Supreme People's Court is inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
